A_target.statement:
Let $C \subseteq \GF q^n$ be a [[Definition:Linear Code|linear $\sqbrk {n, k}$ code]].
Then its [[Definition:Dual Code|dual code]] $C^\perp$ satisfies:
:$\dim C^\perp = n - k$
:$\paren {C^\perp}^\perp = C$

B_source.statement:
Let $V$ be a [[Definition:Vector Space|vector space]] of [[Definition:Dimension of Vector Space|dimension]] $n$ with a [[Definition:Nondegenerate Bilinear Form|nondegenerate bilinear form]].
Let $W \subseteq V$ be a [[Definition:Vector Subspace|subspace]].
Then:
:$\dim W + \dim W^\perp = n$
:$\paren {W^\perp}^\perp = W$

substitutions.the nondegenerate bilinear form: the standard dot product on n-tuples over the finite field

derived.the dimension formula: the dual code has dimension n - k
derived.recovery under double complement: dualizing a code twice returns the original code

validity_conditions: The standard dot product over a finite field is a nondegenerate bilinear form, so the dimension formula applies verbatim.

The form is not positive definite in this setting, so a code can meet its dual nontrivially and self-dual codes exist; the dimension count is unaffected but geometric intuition from the real case does not transfer.
Recovery under double complement requires finite dimension, which holds since the ambient space has n coordinates.
proof_plan: Regard $C$ as a $k$-dimensional [[Definition:Vector Subspace|subspace]] of $\GF q^n$.

The [[Definition:Dot Product|dot product]] $x \cdot y = \displaystyle \sum_i x_i y_i$ is [[Definition:Bilinear Form|bilinear]].
It is [[Definition:Nondegenerate Bilinear Form|nondegenerate]], since $x \cdot e_i = x_i$.

By the source result:
:$\dim C^\perp = n - \dim C = n - k$
